Question: Assume that you are a project manager and you were informed that some of the planned resources to be used in your project will not be available. After rescheduling, you knew that you would run in some delays. The technique you used is called:
Explanation: Resource leveling is a technique in which start and finish dates are adjusted based on resource constraints. Resource leveling can often cause the original critical path to change. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 211.

Question: Assume that you are working on a mega project that would require inputs from various departments in your organization and after you have planned for resources management, a functional manager informed you that he would not be able to assign the planned number of resources to your project; as this department is swamped with work for other projects so, you had to revise your plans to go with the resource constraint imposed by the functional manager. The technique you used is called:
Explanation: A technique in which start and finish dates are adjusted based on resource constraints with the goal of balancing the demand for resources with the available supply. Resource leveling can be used when shared or critically required resources are available only at certain times or in limited quantities, or are over allocated, such as when a resource has been assigned to two or more activities during the same time period, or there is a need to keep resource usage at a constant level. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 211

Question: You are managing a project in the execution phase and all the project progress reports are done on a monthly basis. There were many unplanned vacations during this month so, a delay in the schedule occurred. You decide to check the schedule variance if it is within the allowable threshold. Which document of the following should you refer?
Explanation: The schedule management plan is a component of the project management plan that establishes the criteria and the activities for developing, monitoring, and controlling the schedule. The schedule management plan may be formal or informal, highly detailed, or broadly framed based on the needs of the project, and includes appropriate control thresholds. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 181

Question: In the develop schedule process, ـــــــــــــ technique is used to provide a high-level summary timeline of the 3-6 months schedule based on the product road map and the product vision for the product evaluation.
Explanation: Agile release planning is used in the develop schedule process to provide a high-level summary timeline of the release schedule (3-6) months based on the product roadmap and the product vision for the product evaluation. It also determines the number of iterations or sprints in the release. It also allows the product owner and team to decide how much it needs to be developed and how much it will take to have a releasable product.

Question: A senior management has asked the project manager of a mega project to provide a report containing information on acceptable procurement timetable in addition to assumptions planned for resource allocation. What should the project manager review first to provide this necessary information?
Explanation: The project manager should review procurement management plan to review the timetable of key procurement activities and constraints & assumptions that can affect planned procurements. Since this option is not provided, project management plan is the best answer; as procurement management plan is a subsidiary plan for project management plan. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 466

Question: Christine is a project manager of an underground tunnel project. She is waiting for the clearance to start the construction of her project. This is an example of ___ dependency.
Explanation: External dependencies. External dependencies involve a relationship between project activities and nonproject activities. These dependencies are usually outside of the project team’s control. For example, the testing activity in a software project may be dependent on the delivery of hardware from an external source, or governmental environmental hearings may need to be held before site preparation can begin on a construction project. The project management team determines which dependencies are external during the process of sequencing the activities. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 192

Question: Two developers are about to start implementing two different approved change requests as directed by the project manager. What tool should assist the project team members to know the list of authorized tasks they need to perform?
Explanation: The question states that the project manager has asked two project team members to perform the Direct and Manage Project Work process. Of the options provided, project management information system (PMIS) is the only tool or technique listed. The change log and WBS are inputs to the process, while work performance data is an output. The tool that actually the project team members are required to refer here is the Work Authorization system which is actually a sub-system of PMIS. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 95

Question: Rita is a project manager of an IT development project. The project team members are uncertain about how much time will be needed for each activity. Which of the following techniques is considered the MOST useful?
Explanation: Three-Point Estimating. A technique used to estimate cost or duration by applying an average or weighted average of optimistic, pessimistic, and most likely estimates when there is uncertainty with the individual activity estimates. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 724

Question: You are managing a software research project. Your research officer informs you that you need to plan his research activity so that it finishes before the documentation starts. Other than that, he says it can start as late in the project as necessary. What is the relationship between the research activity and the documentation activity?
Explanation: Finish-to-Start (FS). A logical relationship in which a successor activity cannot start until a predecessor activity has finished. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 707

Question: After estimating all activities durations in your project, you want to determine the group of activities that cannot be delayed or else the project will be delayed. Which of the following tools/techniques should you use?
Explanation: The critical path method is used to estimate the minimum project duration and determine the amount of schedule flexibility on the logical network paths within the schedule model. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 210

Question: You are the project manager of a commercial complex that has to be completed by the end of the year. As you review the remaining work, you discover that there is no way the project will finish on time unless you add extra resources to the work activities. Such planning technique is called:
Explanation: Crashing. A technique used to shorten the schedule duration for the least incremental cost by adding resources. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 703

Question: As a project manager, Daniel has experienced greater than anticipated delays in his current project. To keep the project on schedule, he will need to access the contingency reserves allocated for this risk. What should Daniel do next?
Choice 1: A) Submit a change request to update the schedule baseline.
Choice 2: B) Submit a change request to access the contingency reserves.
Choice 3: C) Take permission from the executive membership team.
Choice 4: D) Access the contingency reserves as needed to meet the project objectives.
Explanation: The project manager manages the schedule and cost reserve and can access the contingency reserves as necessary to meet the project objectives. Since contingency reserves are the estimated duration within the schedule baseline, there is no need to follow formal change control procedure for accessing the contingency reserve. Thus, options A and B are incorrect. Since the project manager manages the schedule/cost baseline and the schedule & cost reserve, option C is not required. Among all options, option D is the best choice.

Question: Assume that your project's activities are as follows: Activity A is the first activity to start with and its duration is 5 weeks. Activities B, C, and D should start after activity A completion and their durations are 5, 7, and 11 weeks respectively. Activity E is dependent on both activities C & D with a duration of 8 weeks. Finally, you have activity F which depends on the completion of both activities B & E with a duration of 3 weeks. What should be the project's critical path?
Explanation: CRITICAL PATH METHOD PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 210

Question: Which of the following tools/techniques might be used during the Control Schedule process in order to analyze and compare actual performance to the approved baselines?
Explanation: Performance reviews measure, compare, and analyze schedule performance against the schedule baseline such as actual start and finish dates, percent complete, and remaining duration for work in progress. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 227

Question: Jane is a Project Manager of a university extension project. Two of her team members are working in a work package. Sales Module which has two activities: Develop Sales Module and Test Sales Module. Both activities have finish-to-start (FS) relationships with zero lead time. What nature of dependencies is existing between the activities Develop Sales Module and the Test Sales Module?
Explanation: The question implies that both activities are involved in finish-to-start relationship and the activity Test Sales Module can only start after Develop Sales Module activity gets finished. It states that both activities have mandatory dependencies among each other. Now, since both activities are project activities and there is no external influence, their relationship is also internal in nature. Therefore, considering all options, C is the best answer. PMBOK guide-6th-edition pages 190, 191

Question: Now, you are developing the project schedule for an obligatory project. You are receiving inputs from different stakeholders and find that many of the stakeholders are estimating the times of completion which are longer than the established end date. What should you do next?
Choice 1: A) Identify a new critical path that could guarantee the completion of the project by the end date.
Choice 2: B) Notify the project sponsor and request to modify the end date to accommodate the proposed schedule.
Choice 3: C) Apply crashing to the project management plan in order to reduce the extension of the proposed schedule.
Choice 4: D) Remind the stakeholders about the project constraints and request a revision of their inputs.
Explanation: Since the inputs of the stakeholders will impact the established end date, the project manager should notify the project sponsor and request to modify the end date to accommodate the proposed schedule.

Question: An activity which is not on the critical path will have a delay of 6 days and it has a float of 4 days. What is the value of total float?
Explanation: Total float = 4-6=-2

Question: As the next milestone approaches in your project, you believe that you will not be able to meet the deadline if the project's performance is kept the same and your project is already over-budget. What should you do?
Explanation: A schedule compression technique in which activities or phases normally done in sequence are performed in parallel for at least a portion of their duration. An example is constructing the foundation for a building before completing all of the architectural drawings. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 215

Question: Charles is managing a renovation of historic building project. He has submitted the cost baseline to the project sponsor. After a review, the project sponsor informs him that the amount he has estimated for a certain month is exceeding the funds that the project sponsor can disburse him for that month. What is the advice that Charles thinks that the project sponsor will give him?
Choice 1: A) To motivate the project team to do the work of that month without being fully paid for it.
Choice 2: B) To reduce the cost estimates of the activities for that month.
Choice 3: C) To reschedule the work of that month.
Choice 4: D) To remove some of the work scope for that month.
Explanation: Rescheduling the work for the period when the funds are lower than estimated will be essential in this scenario. This will require a change request that will impact the cost baseline.

Question: Michael is a project manager of a large multi-year project that is being executed using agile development approach. The project team has used bottom-up estimation for project work related to all near term releases. For all future releases, Michael has created a list of work breakdown structure components above the work package level with known work content, but without detailed schedule activities. What tool or technique has the project team used here? (Choose the BEST answer)
Explanation: As per the mentioned scenario, detailed planning is available for project work that needs to be executed in near term. This can be assumed because the project team used bottom-up estimation technique, which can only be done when work breakdown structure components are decomposed into more detail. The question also states for all future releases only planning packages are planned (Hint: The statement in the question “work breakdown structure components above the work package level with known work content but without detailed schedule activities” signifies the definition of planning packages). This confirms that the project has used Rolling Wave Planning technique. As per definition, rolling wave planning is an iterative planning process which will allow near-term activities to be planned in detail while leaving activities further out planned at a higher level. Thus, among all options provided A is the best answer. PMBOK guide-6th-edition pages 160, 185, 721

Question: You are using a methodology that calculates the amount of float on various paths in the network diagram to determine the minimum project duration. What tool or technique are you using?
Explanation: The critical path method is used to estimate the minimum project duration and determine the amount of schedule flexibility on the logical network paths within the schedule model. A critical path is normally characterized by zero total floats on the critical path.

Question: A project is running using adaptive development approach which has six phases. At the end of second phase, the project goes behind schedule. The finish-to-start relationship between activities of development and testing team is causing the delay. Testing team can only start after development team's work gets completed. The project team, after discussion with experts, decided to adopt test driven development approach for few user stories, where testing and development can go in parallel. This adoption of test driven development is an example of:-
Explanation: Fast tracking. A schedule compression technique in which activities or phases normally done in sequence are performed in parallel for at least a portion of their duration. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 215

Question: Project management team has taken a decision to award the work associated to 4 complex work packages to a preferred vendor. What needs to be reviewed to know when the resources are required to be available for project and when they should be acquired?
Explanation: The situation states that acquire resources process has been performed and a decision has been taken to hire a vendor to work on 4 work packages. Stakeholder register in this scenario may reveal stakeholders needs or expectations for specific resources to be used on the project so, A is incorrect. Resource calendars determine whether resources needed for the project is actually available for the project or not so, B is incorrect. Resource requirements identify which resources are needed to be acquired so, D is also incorrect. The project schedule shows the activities and their planned start and end dates to help determine when the resources need to be available and acquired. Therefore, among all options available, C is best choice. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 331

Question: Due to unexpected weather conditions, your project ran into some delays, and you want to know whether these delays are within the acceptable range or not. What document should you refer to?
Explanation: The schedule management plan may be formal or informal, highly detailed, or broadly framed based on the needs of the project, and includes appropriate control thresholds.

Question: A technique used for constructing a schedule model in which activities are represented by nodes and are graphically linked by one or more logical relationships to show the sequence in which the activities are to be performed is called:
Explanation: Precedence Diagramming Method (PDM). A technique used for constructing a schedule model in which activities are represented by nodes and are graphically linked by one or more logical relationships to show the sequence in which the activities are to be performed. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 714

Question: An output of the Sequence Activities process that is a graphical representation of the logical relationships, also referred to as dependencies, among the project schedule activities is called:
Explanation: A project schedule network diagram is a graphical representation of the logical relationships, also referred to as dependencies, among the project schedule activities. A project schedule network diagram is produced manually or by using project management software. It can include full project details, or have one or more summary activities. A summary narrative can accompany the diagram and describe the basic approach used to sequence the activities. Any unusual activity sequences within the network should be fully described within the narrative. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 194

Question: You are managing a project which will provide e-learning solutions to your customer. The requirements of this project are not clearly defined in the beginning and there will be modifications based on customer feedback as the project evolves. You plan as much as you can and work based on that. You continue the planning as you learn more about the project. Which techniques will be most helpful to define activities on the project?
Explanation: Rolling wave planning is a form of progressive elaboration where work to be accomplished in the near term is planned in detail and future work is planned at a higher level of the WBS. Therefore, work can exist at various levels of detail, depending on where it is in the project life cycle. As more information is known about upcoming events, the near-term higher-level work packages can be decomposed further.

Question: Leo has recently joined a manufacturing project that is in the executing phase as a project manager. He did not find a RAM in the project so, which document should Leo refer to know who is responsible for implementing the work package?
Explanation: The WBS dictionary is a document that provides detailed deliverable, activity, and scheduling information about each component in the WBS. The WBS dictionary is a document that supports the WBS. Most of the information included in the WBS dictionary is created by other processes and added to this document at a later stage. Information in the WBS dictionary may include but is not limited to: Responsible organization. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 162

Question: A management control point where scope, budget, actual cost, and schedule are integrated and compared to earned value for performance measurement is called:-
Explanation: Control accounts are placed at a selected management points of the WBS. Each control account may include one or more work packages, but each of the work packages must be associated with only one control account. PMBOK guide-6th-edition pages 161, 239, 702

Question: You are managing a complex construction project and you request a five-year schedule for this project. In spite of multiple brainstorming sessions with your project team, you struggle to provide details for the project management plan. This causes a delay in obtaining the project management plan approvals. As a project manager, what should you have done to avoid this situation?
Choice 2: B) Used subject matter expert to develop the detailed schedule.
Choice 3: C) Used the rolling wave planning technique for activity planning.
Choice 4: D) Created a high-level Gantt chart to represent the milestone only.
Explanation: The project manager should have used the rolling wave planning technique for activity planning to avoid this situation. Rolling wave planning is an iterative planning technique in which the work to be accomplished in the near term is planned in detail, while work further in the future is planned at a higher level. During early strategic planning when information is less defined, work packages may be decomposed to the known level of detail. As more is known about the upcoming events in the near term, work packages can be decomposed into activities.

Question: Marcelo is a project manager handling a historic building renovation project. During a project performance review with the project team, he notices the following: (a) Activity A, on the critical path, is delayed by 4 days. (b) Activity B, not on the critical path, is delayed by 9 days. (c) Activity C, on the critical path is delayed by 2 days (d) Activity D, not on the critical path, is delayed by 6 days. In what sequence should Marcelo and the project team prioritize their efforts in addressing these delays?
Choice 1: A) Activity B, Activity A, Activity D, Activity C
Choice 2: B) Activity A, Activity C, Activity B, Activity D
Choice 3: C) Activity A, Activity B, Activity D, Activity C
Choice 4: D) Activity B, Activity D, Activity A, Activity C
Explanation: Tasks on critical path should be addressed first, else it may impact the project schedule. Here, of all choices provided, B is the most reasonable choice. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 210

Question: Which of the following is NOT true in relation to critical path?
Choice 1: A) It is the longest path that has the highest total float.
Choice 2: B) It is used to estimate the minimum project duration.
Choice 3: C) Critical paths may have zero or negative float.
Choice 4: D) There can be more than one critical path in a project.
Explanation: B, C, and D are true statements. A is false. The critical path is the sequence of activities that represents the longest path that has the least total float (usually zero) through a project, which determines the shortest possible project duration. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 210

Question: A technique that subdivides the project scope and project deliverables into smaller and more manageable components until the project work associated with accomplishing the project scope is defined in sufficient detail to support executing, monitoring, and controlling the work is also known as:-
Explanation: The question is asking about a technique that will breakdown project scope into more manageable parts, i.e. decomposition. Decomposition helps to create WBS. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 158

Question: Robert is a new project manager of a complex project that is being executed globally. Project team and sponsor are currently engaged in a meeting for a decision in relation to a piece of work. Robert tells everyone that the work associated will be performed from Dubai and type of effort involved in performing the work has already been documented. What did Robert review to address the information stated by him in the meeting?
Explanation: Activity Attributes can be used to identify the place where work has to be performed, the project calendar which the activity is assigned to, and the type of efforts involved. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 186

Question: The project manager and the team decide that the project will be divided into five-week iterations with two weeks in between for retrospectives and iteration planning. Where should this approach be documented?
Explanation: The schedule management plan documents the arrangement and desired designs of the schedules to be used in a project. This includes the timeboxed segments agreed on by the agile team.

Question: In order to make sure that your schedule is flexible enough to handle any unexpected delays as much as possible, you should use:
Explanation: What-if scenario analysis is the process of evaluating scenarios in order to predict their effect, positive or negative, on project objectives. This is an analysis of the question, “What if the situation represented by scenario X happens?” A schedule network analysis is performed using the schedule to compute the different scenarios, such as delaying a major component delivery, extending specific engineering durations, or introducing external factors, such as a strike or a change in the permit process. The outcome of the what-if scenario analysis can be used to assess the feasibility of the project schedule under different conditions, and in preparing schedule reserves and response plans to address the impact of unexpected situations. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 213.

Question: Anthony is managing a construction project that is 2 months behind, but is surprisingly marked under budget. Anthony decided to try to make up time, but needs to minimize the project risk. What is the best thing to do?
Explanation: Crashing may be performed; as the project is within budget. Crashing usually incurs an extra cost. Fast-tracking will increase the risk so, it is not an option.

Question: Assume that you are the project manager of a road renovation project, and after the beginning of the execution, you discovered that some activities need to be rescheduled; as their planned resources would not fit because the site area is limited by the ongoing traffic. What should you do?
Explanation: Resource leveling. A technique in which start and finish dates are adjusted based on resource constraints with the goal of balancing the demand for resources with the available supply. Resource leveling can be used when shared or critically required resources are available only at certain times or in limited quantities, or are over-allocated such as when a resource has been assigned to two or more activities during the same time period or there is a need to keep resource usage at a constant level. Resource leveling can often cause the original critical path to change. Available float is used for leveling resources. Consequently, the critical path through the project schedule may change. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 211

Question: You are working on a project that consists of three releases, five iterations per release. The first release will provide the must-have features required for a minimum viable product with additional features added after each subsequent release. The customer wants to know which features will be available at the end of each iteration. What is the best tool or technique to use in this situation?
Explanation: Agile release planning provides a high-level summary timeline of the release schedule and defines which features will be available at the end of each iteration.

Question: Lucy is the new project manager of a software development project who has joined during execution. The project is getting executed using agile development approach where scope of work gets progressively elaborated. She wants to review the remaining scope of work which is not decomposed to the lowest level, but has known work content. What should she review to get this necessary information?
Choice 1: A) Review the project management plan.
Choice 2: B) Review all control accounts in WBS.
Choice 3: C) Review the planning packages which are yet to be decomposed further.
Choice 4: D) Review the project scope statement.
Explanation: A planning package is a WBS component below the control account and above the work package with known work content and without detailed scheduled activities. In a project, where scope gets progressively elaborated, planning packages are decomposed later to work package level when greater amounts of information and more accurate estimates become available. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 161

Question: A project manager estimates the work to be accomplished in the near term in detail at a low level of the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS). He estimates work far in the future as WBS components that are at a relatively high level of the WBS. This technique is called:
Explanation: Rolling Wave Planning. An iterative planning technique in which the work to be accomplished in the near term is planned in detail, while the work in the future is planned at a higher level. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 721

Question: Christina is a project manager who is using an approach that calculates the amount of float on several paths in the network diagram to determine the minimum project duration. What tool or technique is she using?
Explanation: The critical path method is used to estimate the minimum project duration and determine the amount of schedule flexibility on the logical network paths within the schedule model. This schedule network analysis technique calculates the early start, early finish, late start, and late finish dates for all activities without regard for any resource limitations by performing a forward and backward pass analysis through the schedule network. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 210

Question: Recently, you have been assigned to a new project in the execution phase and you are responsible for the execution of certain activities and you want to better understand the activities and their chronological order. Which of the following documents should assist you?
Explanation: Activity attributes extend the description of the activity by identifying multiple components associated with each activity. The components for each activity evolve over time. During the initial stages of the project, they include the unique activity identifier (ID), WBS ID, and activity label or name. When completed, they may include activity descriptions, predecessor activities, successor activities, logical relationships, leads and lags. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 186

Question: Emily is managing a store expansion project. She uses the schedule from a similar project to estimate the cost of this project activities. Which method did she use to derive the estimates?
Explanation: Analogous Estimating. A technique for estimating the duration or cost of an activity or a project using historical data from a similar activity or project. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 699

Question: Peter is managing a complex residential compound project. He requests a five-year schedule for this project. Despite the fact that there were multi brainstorming sessions with the project team, he struggles to provide details for the project management plan and this caused a delay in obtaining the approval of the project management plan. What should Peter have done to avoid this situation?
Choice 1: A) Created a high level Gantt chart representing the milestone only.
Choice 2: B) Used the rolling wave planning technique for activity planning.
Choice 4: D) Used subject matter expert to develop the detailed schedule.
Explanation: Rolling Wave Planning. An iterative planning technique in which the work to be accomplished in the near term is planned in detail, while the work in the future is planned at a higher level. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 721

Question: Assume that you are the project manager of a railway construction project and your team has finished defining all project activities and you are now starting the Sequence Activities process. You find that most construction activities are sequential so, you suggest to use a technique that links activities through logical relationships where the start or the finish of an activity depends on its predecessor. What technique are you suggesting to use?
Explanation: The precedence diagramming method (PDM) is a technique used for constructing a schedule model in which activities are represented by nodes and are graphically linked by one or more logical relationships to show the sequence in which the activities are to be performed. PDM includes four types of dependencies or logical relationships. A predecessor activity is an activity that logically comes before a dependent activity in a schedule. A successor activity is a dependent activity that logically comes after another activity in a schedule. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 189

Question: Silvana is managing a multi-task project in which task B is dependent on task A that is delayed. The project resources for task B have limited availability and should begin task B on time. What should Silvana do to re-plan the schedule to keep the deadline unchanged?
Choice 1: A) Fast track task A and move the start date of task B.
Choice 2: B) Fast track task B and begin the work immediately.
Choice 3: C) Crash task A and start task B on the planned time.
Choice 4: D) Replan the start date of task B so it begins after the completion of task A.
Explanation: The relation between task A and task B is FS. Since task A is delayed, the project manager should crash task A and start task B on the planned time to keep the deadline unchanged. Option A is not correct; as this will change the deadline. Option B is not correct; as the resources of task B have limited availability. Option D is not correct; as this will change the deadline.

Question: You are a project manager of a construction project and during a presentation to the senior management, you want to display the project schedule and only the key deliverables to be displayed. What is the correct tool you are going to use to achieve this?
Explanation: Milestone charts. These charts are similar to bar charts, but only identify the scheduled start or completion of major deliverables and key external interfaces. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 218

Question: During the last progress meeting, you informed the sponsor that the project status is "under budget and behind schedule" and you might fail to achieve the project requirements regarding the finish date if the progress remains the same. If you know that the remaining activities must be performed sequentially, what should you do to meet the project's requirements?
Choice 2: B) Cancel the delayed parts of the works.
Choice 4: D) Study the possibility of using fast track method.
Explanation: A technique used to shorten the schedule duration for the least incremental cost by adding resources. Examples of crashing include approving overtime, bringing in additional resources, or paying to expedite delivery to activities on the critical path. Crashing works only for activities on the critical path where additional resources will shorten the activity’s duration. Crashing does not always produce a viable alternative and may result in increased risk and/or cost. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 215

Question: While working in the Define Activities process, you discovered that the final work package drawings have not been issued yet. You raised the issue to your manager and he advised you to start with ready packages and assume a high level planning for that final package. Such a technique is called:
Explanation: Rolling wave planning is an iterative planning technique in which the work to be accomplished in the near term is planned in detail, while work further in the future is planned at a higher level. PMBOK guide-6th-edition page 185.
